referents.why: him (auton, masculine singular) is the object of Pilate's questioning, Jesus; Pilate is the speaker
You (Su) in Pilate's question is second person, addressed to Jesus as addressee of that speech
to him (auto) in the reply: Jesus answers Pilate, the addressee of the reply
You have said so is Jesus' reply to Pilate; second person singular, so Pilate is the addressee

links.why: Pilate's question is what he said; the asking verb takes it as content (R1), not a separate and
questioned him: the question Are you the King of the Jews is what is said (R1)
the reply follows the question in the dialogue sequence
participle answering to him is nested in the reply verb
the words said are the content of the reply (R1), not a grammatical nesting
Jesus says You have said so: the saying clause has its said clause as content (R1)
reversed: the reply comes after the question, not before it

groups.why: Pilate's question: frame is the asking, part the question, sender Pilate; addressee Jesus added
Jesus' reply: builder's sender w12 is not a candidate here; the speaker is Jesus, addressee Pilate. cl3 (answering to him) describes the reply rather than saying it, so it is no longer a part

cant_tell.what: whether answering to him (cl3) belongs to the turn
cant_tell.why: a turn has one frame, and the participle describes the act of replying rather than being said; left outside the turn as a within clause for review
